es: Mediar en un desacuerdo: resumir las posturas con equilibrio, reformular emociones sin culpar, proponer una salida y fijar por escrito lo acordado.

teaching.en: As the mediator, I will stay impartial and summarise both positions fairly before we look for a solution.
teaching.es: Como mediadora, me mantendré imparcial y resumiré ambas posturas con equidad antes de buscar una solución.
teaching.explanationEs: Un resumen equilibrado da a cada persona su postura, con el mismo peso.
segments: As the mediator, I will stay impartial and summarise
both positions fairly before we look for a solution.

teaching.en: Let me summarise: Ana needs quiet evenings to rest, and Tom needs time to practise, so each of you has a valid point.
teaching.es: Déjame resumir: Ana necesita tardes tranquilas para descansar y Tom necesita tiempo para practicar, así que cada uno tiene una parte de razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Let me summarise + las necesidades de cada uno: sin adjetivos que tomen partido.
segments: Let me summarise: Ana needs quiet evenings to rest, and Tom needs
time to practise, so each of you has a valid point.

teaching.en: It seems you both want to feel respected in your own home, and that common ground is worth building on.
teaching.es: Parece que los dos quieren sentirse respetados en su propia casa, y ese terreno común merece construirse.
teaching.explanationEs: It seems you both want...: señala lo que tienen en común antes de negociar.
segments: It seems you both want to feel respected in your
own home, and that common ground is worth building on.

teaching.en: I am here to mediate, not to take sides, and the sticking point seems to be Sunday lunch.
teaching.es: Estoy aquí para mediar, no para tomar partido, y el punto de fricción parece ser el almuerzo del domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: El mediador no decide quién tiene razón: identifica el punto de fricción y ayuda a resolverlo.
segments: I am here to mediate, not to take sides,
and the sticking point seems to be Sunday lunch.

teaching.en: What if we try a compromise for two weeks? And could we agree to review it together on Sunday?
teaching.es: ¿Y si probamos un acuerdo con cesiones durante dos semanas? ¿Y podríamos acordar revisarlo juntos el domingo?
teaching.explanationEs: What if...? y Could we agree...? proponen una salida sin imponerla; review fija cuándo se comprueba.

could we agree to review it together on Sunday?

teaching.en: So we settle on this: music until ten, a neutral tone when we disagree, and we put in writing exactly what we agreed.
teaching.es: Así que fijamos esto: música hasta las diez, un tono neutral cuando no estemos de acuerdo, y dejamos por escrito exactamente lo que acordamos.
teaching.explanationEs: So we agreed that...: repite lo pactado; ponerlo por escrito evita dudas más tarde.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del mediador resume las dos posturas con equilibrio?

choices.text: Ana needs quiet evenings, but Tom only thinks about his music and his friends.
Tom needs time to practise, so Ana should rest somewhere else.
Ana needs quiet evenings to rest, and Tom needs time to practise.

feedback.es: El resumen equilibrado da a cada persona su necesidad con el mismo peso, sin adjetivos que juzguen.

hint.es: Busca la frase que da a cada uno su necesidad, sin juzgar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Déjame resumir lo que he oído hasta ahora.»

feedback.es: Summarise es resumir; Let me summarise abre un resumen equilibrado antes de proponer una salida.

hint.es: Es el verbo inglés para «resumir»; no es resume.

origin.text: The mediator wants both sides to feel heard before she proposes anything. She says: Let me ___ what I have heard so far.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Y si probamos un acuerdo durante dos semanas?»

answer.text: What if we try a compromise for two weeks

feedback.es: What if abre una propuesta sin imponerla; compromise es el acuerdo con cesiones.

hint.es: Empieza por What if y termina con el plazo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hizo la mediadora antes de proponer una salida.

choices.text: She summarised both positions and pointed out what they shared.
She asked the son to explain why he rarely came home.
She told the mother that her son was right to go out.

feedback.es: La mediadora resume ambas posturas y subraya lo común (querer sentirse respetados) antes de proponer.

origin.audio: In a workshop for volunteer mediators, the trainer described a family argument over Sunday lunches. The mother wanted everyone at the table, while her son wanted time with his friends. The mediator stayed neutral. She summarised both positions, pointing out that they both wanted to feel respected. Then she asked: What if we try a compromise? The son would come twice a month, and the family would choose the dates together. Everyone agreed to review the plan after two months.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige en qué consistía el compromiso.

choices.text: The son would come every week, but he would leave early after the main dish.
The son would come to lunch twice a month, on dates chosen together.
The mother would stop organising Sunday lunches for good.

feedback.es: El compromiso reparte las cesiones: el hijo viene dos veces al mes y las fechas se eligen entre todos.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un buen mediador no toma partido: ayuda a ambos a encontrar una solución.»

feedback.es: Take sides significa tomar partido por una persona; el mediador se mantiene imparcial.

origin.text: Some people think that a mediator decides who is right. In fact, a good mediator does not ___ sides: she helps both people find a solution.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje final de la mediación a Ana y Leo.

answer.text:
Dear Ana and Leo,
Thank you both for talking so openly today. Let me summarise what I heard. Ana, it sounds like you feel overwhelmed when the Sunday plans change at the last minute, and you need to know earlier. Leo, what I'm hearing is that you feel left out when you cannot see your friends, and you need some free time. Neither of you is wrong: you both want a calm weekend and to feel respected.
What if we try a compromise? Leo will tell Ana by Friday evening if he has other plans. Ana will keep Sunday lunch free until then, and she will not ask him to cancel later. If either of you feels upset, please say it with an I-message, for example, I feel frustrated when...
So we agreed that we will follow this plan for two weeks. Let's review it next Sunday, and we can change anything that does not work.
Thank you both for your honesty and your patience. I am proud of how you listened to each other.
Mia

What if we try a compromise? Leo will tell Ana by Friday evening if he has other plans. Ana will keep Sunday lunch free until then, and she will not ask him to cancel later. If either of you feels upset, please say it with an I-message, for example, I feel frustrated when...
So we agreed that we will follow this plan for two weeks. Let's review it next Sunday, and we can change anything that does not work.
Thank you both for your honesty and your patience. I am proud of how you listened to each other.

Hi Ana and Leo,
I'm glad we talked. To summarise: Ana, it sounds like you feel stressed because the plans for Sunday lunch change suddenly, and you need time to organise. Leo, it sounds like you feel frustrated because you rarely see your friends, and you need space. I think you both want the same thing, which is a peaceful home where everybody feels heard.
Could we agree on a simple solution? Leo will tell Ana by Friday whether he is free on Sunday. In return, Ana will not plan the lunch until she hears from him. If there is a problem, we will speak calmly and take a break first.
So we agreed that this starts this week. We will check in again in two weeks, and then we will decide if we keep it.
Thanks for listening to each other. I'm proud of both of you, and I hope that the plan makes Sundays calmer and happier for everybody in the family. If either of you feels upset before then, please say it with an I-message and we will talk.
Mia

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje de mediación resume las dos posturas con equilibrio, reformula emociones, propone una salida y fija el acuerdo y su revisión.

origin.text: Ana se siente agobiada cuando Leo cambia a última hora los planes del domingo y necesita saberlo antes. Leo se siente excluido cuando no puede ver a sus amigos y necesita tiempo libre. Como mediador, escribe un mensaje a los dos (unas 150–270 palabras): resume ambas posturas con equilibrio, reformula sus emociones sin culpar, propone una salida con What if o Could we agree, y fija lo acordado y su revisión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la mediadora pregunta a Leo si algo le parece injusto.

choices.text: Because Leo had refused to sign the agreement earlier in the same meeting.
Because she wants to change the plan before it starts.
Because his body language suggests a doubt that he has not voiced.

feedback.es: Leo mira al suelo y duda; la mediadora lo nota y le da espacio para decir lo que no ha dicho.

origin.audio: Ana and Leo had both agreed to the plan, but the mediator noticed that Leo kept looking at the floor. Before closing the meeting she asked him: Is there anything that still feels unfair? Leo hesitated, then said that he would accept the plan, but he was not sure that Ana would keep her side. The mediator wrote that down and suggested a review in two weeks.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige para qué sirve la revisión dentro de dos semanas.

choices.text: To check whether Ana keeps her side and adjust the plan if needed.
To let Leo choose a new plan without talking to Ana about it first.
To decide which of the two people was wrong.

feedback.es: La revisión responde a la duda de Leo: se comprueba el acuerdo y se ajusta si hace falta, sin buscar culpables.

prompt.es: Completa: «El principal punto de fricción parece ser el almuerzo del domingo.»

feedback.es: Sticking point es el punto de fricción: lo que impide cerrar un acuerdo.

origin.text: Both of them agree on the chores and on the music. The main sticking ___ seems to be Sunday lunch.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje del mediador y elige qué evita hacer.

choices.text: It avoids mentioning what either of them feels.
It avoids saying which of the two people is to blame.
It avoids proposing a date to check the plan again with both of them.

feedback.es: El mensaje nombra emociones y propone revisar el domingo, pero no dice quién tiene la culpa: mediación imparcial.

origin.text: Hi both, thanks for today. I hear that you both want a calm home. Ana, it sounds like you feel tired when the plans change; Leo, it seems you feel left out. So, could we agree that Leo tells Ana by Friday, and that we review this next Sunday?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir la mediadora con su última frase.

choices.text: That the compromise failed because nobody was happy.
That mediators should make both sides unhappy on purpose, to be fair.
That a fair deal means that each side gives up something.

feedback.es: «Slightly unhappy but respected» resume la idea: en un buen compromiso cada parte cede algo sin perder el respeto.

origin.audio: After two hours of arguing, the brother and sister finally agreed on a plan. Nobody won completely: she gave up her Sunday dinners twice a month, and he promised to call every Friday. The mediator said that a good compromise leaves both people slightly unhappy but respected.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un mediador debe ser imparcial: si toma partido, nadie confiará en ella.»

feedback.es: Impartial describe a quien no favorece a ninguna parte; sin imparcialidad, el mediador pierde la confianza.

origin.text: A mediator must stay ___. If she takes sides, nobody will trust her.
